The **upwind DG semidiscretization** seeks a differentiable cellwise polynomial $u_h(t)$ such that for every $K\in\mathcal T_h$ and $v_h\in\mathbb P_p(K)$,
$$\int_K (\partial_tu_h)v_h\,dx-\int_K \beta u_h\cdot\nabla v_h\,dx+\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\int_F\widehat f_{K,F}v_h\,dS=0.$$
$$\int_K\operatorname{div}G\,dx=\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\int_FG\cdot n_{K,F}\,dS.$$

In the sum of the oriented boundaries of all top-dimensional cells, every interior
facet occurs twice with opposite signs; every boundary facet occurs once.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

derivations.claim: In the DG equation on each cell take $v=u_h$. The time term is $\frac12\frac{d}{dt}\|u_h\|_{L^2(K)}^2$. Since $\beta$ is constant, $-\int_K\beta u_h\cdot\nabla u_h=-\frac12\int_K\operatorname{div}(\beta u_h^2)=-\frac12\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\int_F(\beta\cdot n_{K,F})u_h^2$ by [F2] and [A1]. Sum over cells; [F3] pairs the two opposite normals on each interior facet.

Fix an interior facet oriented from $K^-$ to $K^+$ and put $b=\beta\cdot n_F$. The two face terms from step 1.1 and the two upwind numerical-flux terms combine to $-\frac b2((u^-)^2-(u^+)^2)+b\widehat u(u^--u^+)$. If $b>0$, then $\widehat u=u^-$ and this is $\frac b2(u^+-u^-)^2$; if $b<0$, then $\widehat u=u^+$ and this is $\frac{|b|}{2}(u^+-u^-)^2$. For $b=0$ it vanishes.

On an outflow boundary face, $b=\beta\cdot n>0$ and $\widehat u=u_h$, so the volume and flux terms combine to $\frac b2u_h^2$. On an inflow face, $b<0$ and $\widehat u=g$, so they combine to $\frac{|b|}{2}u_h^2-|b|gu_h=\frac{|b|}{2}(u_h-g)^2-\frac{|b|}{2}g^2$. Faces with $b=0$ contribute zero.

Substituting the interior contribution from step 2.1 and the boundary contributions from step 2.2 into the sum of the tested DG equations gives the displayed identity. All terms on the left after the time derivative are nonnegative; setting $g=0$ proves the final stability statement.

derivations.claim: Choose the finite monomial basis $\{\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_M\}$ of $\mathbb P_p(K)$. Its Gram matrix $G_{ij}=\int_K\phi_i\phi_j\,d\mu$ is positive definite: for every nonzero coefficient vector $c$, the polynomial $q=\sum_i c_i\phi_i$ is continuous and nonzero at some point of $K$, so it is bounded away from zero on a nonempty relatively open subset; full support gives $c^TGc=\int_Kq^2\,d\mu>0$. Each moment $b_i=\int_Ku\phi_i\,d\mu$ is finite by [F2]. The invertible system $Gc=b$ therefore has a unique solution, and $p=\sum_i c_i\phi_i$ satisfies [F1].

For any $w\in\mathbb P_p(K)$, write $u-w=(u-\Pi_Ku)+(\Pi_Ku-w)$. The first term is orthogonal to the second by [F1], hence $\|u-w\|_2^2=\|u-\Pi_Ku\|_2^2+\|\Pi_Ku-w\|_2^2\ge\|u-\Pi_Ku\|_2^2$. Taking square roots proves best approximation.

citations.quote:
The **degree-zero upwind forward-Euler update** is admissible when $\lambda_K\le1$ for every cell; its output is
$$U_K^+=U_K-\frac{\Delta t}{V_K}\sum_{F\subset\partial K}A_F\widehat f_{K,F}.$$
$$\int_K\operatorname{div}G\,dx=\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\int_FG\cdot n_{K,F}\,dS.$$

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

derivations.claim: By [F2] with the constant vector field $\beta$, $\sum_FA_Fb_{K,F}=0$, hence $\sum_FA_F(-b_{K,F})^+=\sum_FA_Fb_{K,F}^+$. Rewriting [F1] gives $U_K^+=(1-\lambda_K)U_K+\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\frac{\Delta tA_F(-b_{K,F})^+}{V_K}U_{K_F}$. All coefficients are nonnegative by $\lambda_K\le1$, and their sum is $(1-\lambda_K)+\lambda_K=1$.

Convexity of $\eta$ and the convex-combination formula in step 1.1 give $V_K\eta(U_K^+)\le V_K(1-\lambda_K)\eta(U_K)+\Delta t\sum_FA_F(-b_{K,F})^+\eta(U_{K_F})$. Sum over cells. Each incoming coefficient for an upwind cell $J$ is paired with the equal outgoing coefficient $\Delta tA_Fb_{J,F}^+$ on that same periodic face, so these terms exactly fill the subtracted $V_J\lambda_J\eta(U_J)$ contributions. Therefore $\sum_KV_K\eta(U_K^+)\le\sum_KV_K\eta(U_K)$.

Multiply the update [F1] by $V_K$ and sum over cells. Every periodic interior face contributes one shared flux with each of its two opposite outward normals, so its two signed contributions cancel. This proves $\sum_KV_KU_K^+=\sum_KV_KU_K$.

Because each cell is a nondegenerate simplex, it is the closure of its nonempty Euclidean interior. Every nonempty relatively open subset of a cell therefore intersects that interior in a nonempty Euclidean-open set, which contains a Euclidean ball. By [F5] and [A1] the ball has positive measure, so Lebesgue measure has full support on each cell.
The full-support condition in step 1.2 lets us invoke the cellwise projection lemma [F7] on every cell, so $\Pi_hu$ is well defined.

Set $	heta=u_h-\Pi_hu$, so $u_h-u=	heta+\eta$. Subtract the exact weak equation in step 1.1 from [F1] and test with $v_h=	heta$. Differentiating projection orthogonality in [F2] on the fixed mesh gives $(\eta_t,	heta)_K=0$. If $p=0$, then $
abla	heta=0$; if $p\ge1$, then $
abla	heta\in\mathbb P_{p-1}(K)^d$. Since $ eta$ is constant, in either case $ eta\cdot
abla	heta\in\mathbb P_p(K)$ and $(\eta, eta\cdot
abla	heta)_K=0$. This leaves only the transport error and the upwind face-flux differences.

Integrate the remaining $-(\beta\theta,\nabla\theta)_K$ by parts using [F3] and sum over cells using [F4]. At an interior face the homogeneous upwind terms combine to $\frac12\int_F|\beta\cdot n_F|[\theta]^2$; at inflow the volume term is $\frac12\int_{\Gamma_-}|\beta\cdot n|\theta^2$, and at outflow the homogeneous term is $\frac12\int_{\Gamma_+}(\beta\cdot n)\theta^2$. By the face flux differences from step 3.1, inflow contributes no projection residual because both fluxes use $g$; interior and outflow residuals move to the right with signs $+\int_F(\beta\cdot n_F)\eta^{\mathrm{up}}[\theta]$ and $-\int_{\Gamma_+}(\beta\cdot n)\eta\theta$, respectively. Hence
$$\frac12\frac d{dt}\|\theta\|_2^2+\frac12\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^{\mathrm{int}}}\int_F|\beta\cdot n_F|[\theta]^2+\frac12\int_{\Gamma_-}|\beta\cdot n|\theta^2+\frac12\int_{\Gamma_+}(\beta\cdot n)\theta^2=\sum_{F\in\mathcal F_h^{\mathrm{int}}}\int_F(\beta\cdot n_F)\eta^{\mathrm{up}}[\theta]-\int_{\Gamma_+}(\beta\cdot n)\eta\theta.$$

For each interior face use $|b||\eta^{\mathrm{up}}||[\theta]|\le\frac{|b|}{4}[\theta]^2+|b||\eta^{\mathrm{up}}|^2$, and on outflow use $b|\eta||\theta|\le\frac b4\theta^2+b|\eta|^2$. Absorbing the first terms into the half-dissipation terms of step 4.1 and dropping the remaining nonnegative boundary and jump terms gives $\frac d{dt}\|\theta\|_2^2\le2R_h(t)^2$.
Integrating the differential inequality gives $\|\theta(T)\|_2^2\le\|\theta(0)\|_2^2+2\int_0^TR_h(t)^2dt$. Since $u_h-u=\theta+\eta$, the triangle inequality at $T$ gives the stated estimate.

The second sum is $\sum_F\sum_q\omega_{F,q}v(U_{F,q})^TF_{n_F}(U_{F,q})$ by [F2], diagonal face selection, and consistency from [F4]. Summing directions and the potential identity in [F3] proves the volume entropy boundary identity.

The chain rule gives $\frac{d}{dt}\sum_iH_{ii}\eta(U_i)=\sum_iH_{ii}v(U_i)^T\dot U_i$. Since the semidiscrete equation is $H\dot U+V+SAT=0$, the entropy rate is the negative of the volume and SAT contractions. Combining the volume contraction from step 1.1 with $-v^TR^TM(\widehat F_n^*-F_n)$ cancels the physical flux and leaves, on each cell face, $\sum_q\omega_{F,q}(\psi_{n_F}(U_{F,q})-v(U_{F,q})^T\widehat F_{n_F,q}^*)$.

Sum the cell entropy rates from step 2.1. By [F5] the two cell contributions at an interior face can be written in one orientation as $-[\psi_n]+[v]^T\widehat F_{n,F,q}^*$. Substitution of the flux definition in [F1] and the directional jump identity [F4] makes this $-\alpha_{F,q}\lVert[v]\rVert^2/2$. The boundary-cell contributions are $-\mathcal B_h$ by definition. Moving these terms to the left gives the asserted identity, and [A1] gives nonincrease.

For each component, the constant-vector contraction of the volume term is $2\sum_{i,j}Q_{ij}F^{ec}(U_i,U_j)=\sum_{i,j}(Q_{ij}+Q_{ji})F^{ec}(U_i,U_j)$. The SBP identity and diagonal face selection [F2] reduce this to the physical normal-flux quadrature on the cell boundary, since consistency of the directional fluxes in [F4] gives $F^{ec}(U_i,U_i)=F(U_i)$. The constant-vector contraction of the SAT [F1] subtracts that physical flux and leaves only the numerical normal-flux quadrature. Its interior contributions cancel by normal reversal from the interface formula [F1]; identified periodic boundary partners cancel in the same way. Therefore the periodic quadrature-weighted total state is constant.

For every convex function $\eta:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, the weighted discrete entropy does not increase:
$$\sum_KV_K\eta(U_K^+)\le\sum_KV_K\eta(U_K).$$

If $\Phi:C\to\mathbb R$ is convex, meaning $\Phi(\theta u+(1-\theta)v)\le\theta\Phi(u)+(1-\theta)\Phi(v)$ for $u,v\in C$ and $0\le\theta\le1$, and $\Phi(E_h(u))\le\Phi(u)$ for every $u\in C$, then $\Phi$ does not increase at any of the three stages or at the output.
A subset $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ is **convex** when, for all $x,y\in U$ and $t\in[0,1]$ ([[def-interval]]), the point $(1-t)x+ty$ lies in $U$.
The function $f:C\to\mathbb R$ is convex when $f((1-t)x+ty)\le(1-t)f(x)+tf(y)$ for all $x,y\in C$ and $t\in[0,1]$.

The **degree-zero upwind forward-Euler update** is admissible when $\lambda_K\le1$ for every cell; its output is
$$U_K^+=U_K-\frac{\Delta t}{V_K}\sum_{F\subset\partial K}A_F\widehat f_{K,F}.$$

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

derivations.claim: By [F1], the spatially autonomous SSPRK(3,3) step has exactly the three displayed convex-combination stages. Set $C=\mathbb R^{\mathcal T_h}$ and $\Phi(U)=\sum_KV_K\eta(U_K)$. For $U,V\in C$ and $0\le t\le1$, apply [F5] in each cell and multiply by $V_K>0$ from [F6]; summing proves convexity of $\Phi$.

The state space $C$ is convex and $\Phi$ is convex. By [F2], every forward-Euler image of a cell-state vector lies in $C$ and has no larger $\Phi$ value under the assumed cell CFL. Thus the hypotheses of the convex-transfer clause [F3] hold at the same $\Delta t$.

Applying [F3] to the three stages in [F1] gives $\Phi(U^{n+1})\le\Phi(U^n)$, which is the asserted weighted entropy inequality. The flux-differencing semidiscrete entropy theorem is not used in this transfer.

derivations.claim: For the central flux, both faces of cell 1 see the same pair $(u_1,u_2)$ and hence the same flux; likewise for cell 2. Thus $\dot u_1=\dot u_2=0$ and $E=\frac h2(u_1^2+u_2^2)$ has $\dot E=0$.
